title: The 4-Tier Memory Architecture
use_cases: Use when maintaining narrative consistency across multiple chapters
Configure when balancing token window constraints with long-term plot awareness
Implement when automated character and location tracking is required for evolving drafts
Use when setting up an iterative critique-and-regeneration workflow for content quality
Configure when needing to strip dialogue while preserving core story beats for memory efficiency
content:
After every chapter, we update the Rolling Summary:

- Recent Chapters (High Fidelity): last 1–3 chapters with vivid detailIf someone is bleeding in Chapter 19, they should still be injured in Chapter 20.
- Short-Term Memory (Medium Fidelity): the current arc’s key beats and decisions (dialogue stripped)
- Long-Term Memory (Low Fidelity): heavily compressed macro-events that still matter
- Dynamic Entity Registry: tracks newly introduced characters/places/items so they don’t vanish or mutate

(We keep the entity registry logic high-level here, implementation details vary, but the main point is: new, on the fly entities are captured immediately.)

Drafting also runs as an iterative loop:

1. Generate chapter draft
2. Critique against artifacts + rolling summary + outline
3. Regenerate with critique(Rubric metrics)
4. Repeat until approval or max recursion depth
